naval: Context-only classification applies to all institutions here: research, classified work, naval intelligence, and acoustic or radar surveillance do not establish UAP involvement.

The Navy/NSA/NRO/CIA official hosts repeatedly returned 403, 404 or fetch errors. Accessible official DVIDS copies, archived official pages and explicitly labeled scholarly/publication mirrors were used. No inaccessible source supports a final record.

NURO exists in inspected first-person oral history and scholarly literature. Its exact founding agreement, governance charter, first official acknowledgment and declassification date remain separate unresolved questions.
NSDM 40 names a National Underwater Reconnaissance Program. It is not silently equated with the Office or treated as a 1970 founding charter.
CIA Studies in Intelligence September 2023 is a review venue. Its NURO book-review mention is evidence of public reference only, subject to the review disclaimer.
Only selected passages of archival guides and long documents were inspected. Finding-aid descriptions do not equal inspection of the underlying collections.
ONI, NISC, the NMIC facility, the 2009 NMIC organization and its 2012 NMIO name are intentionally separate; co-location and shared leadership do not merge their identities.
Verified year/month/range precision is preserved. Unknown founding, rename or disclosure days are not filled with January 1 dates.
NOSC/NCCOSC/NRaD and SPAWAR/NAVWAR are different organizational levels. This packet does not invent a complete 1992–2008 Point Loma succession from partial evidence.
Mission descriptions are tied to the inspected publication era and should not be treated as a current inventory of capabilities or classified responsibilities.
space: This is a targeted passage and scanned-page review, not a complete audit of NRO, Air Force or classified archives.
Many official .mil URLs returned 403 despite indexed text. Opened GovInfo and DVIDS mirrors provide support; inaccessible search snippets do not.
Formation, authorization, first flight, first successful imagery, closure, internal declassification and public announcement are different event types.
Preserve the original 1961 NRO letter’s unimplemented co-directorship caveat. Later institutional histories sometimes recount co-directors without that qualification.
The 2005 POPPY release incorrectly dates NRO formation to 1962; it is used only for POPPY public recognition.
The NRO 50-year history conflates the 1974 Program D closure with A-12 deactivation. Only closure and asset transfer are adopted.
Parent-unit titles of the alphabet offices changed. Later CIA OSP/OD&E/DS&T titles must not be retrojected into 1962. Detailed office chronology awaits inspected original records.
NOSS/White Cloud naming and scope remain unresolved from opened primary records. This is an evidence gap, not proof of nonexistence.

PARCAE support is a visually inspected 2023 prepared speech reproduced in a 2026 Senate volume. It does not establish exactly what was delivered orally. The original public release and internal approval memo were inaccessible.
Dated radar/operator accounts from 2018–2023 must not be presented as unchanged current 2026 organization.
Original operational dates for BMEWS, PAVE PAWS and PARCS were not established in this pass; supported mission profiles are included without invented dates.
Institutional secrecy and sensor capabilities alone do not establish UAP retrieval, reverse engineering or concealment. No adopted source here establishes exotic origin.
External relationship endpoints usaf, cia, nrl, nsa and us-strategic-command should resolve to canonical entities from the parent or other packets.

October 1979, March 1989 and July 1992 acquisition-lineage milestones now use month precision from opened official sources. A private AFHRA-attributed transcription remains in the research ledger but does not supply adopted exact-day claims.
intelligence: The official 18-member IC roster was fully screened; only the scoped intelligence/technical/UAP institutions received substantive history review. A roster entry is not evidence of a UAP program.

No claim of exhaustive CIA Reading Room, FOIA corpus, congressional record, YouTube channel or classified-record review. Several CIA Reading Room URLs redirected to the homepage; inspected original mirrors are identified individually.

Institutional histories can contain shorthand and disagreements. AAWSAP original September 22, 2008 contract predates AARO’s 2009 phrasing; CSS 1971 authorization differs from agency 1972 establishment year; Grudge first closure dates conflict.

The ATIC/FTD/NASIC chain has inspected private institutional-history support, while original Air Force lineage pages were blocked. Treat its exact-day dates as provisional for integration until a primary source is retrieved.

Formation, authorization, operational start, rename, termination, release approval and public-disclosure dates are kept distinct; an internal record is not presented as public knowledge on its creation date.

OGA office identity is corroborated by biographies; its alleged UAP recovery role is separate. Immaculate Constellation and MJ-12 are claims/provenance cases. Lack of retrieved public records alone is not proof of nonexistence.
KONA BLUE’s prospective SAP is documented; approval of a security compartment did not approve the proposed operational SAP, establish a funded recovery mission, or authenticate assumed materials.
NARA, CIA, ODNI, FBI and congressional custody are provenance facts, not automatic endorsement of all submitted assertions. Agency assessments and witness statements are attributed to their authors.
Relationship edges represent documented institutional actions only; no edge is inferred from shared personnel, proximity, a common contractor, or a speaker’s UAP hypothesis.
No blanket FOIA or secrecy exemption claims are drawn. Specific release letters describe only the records and determinations in those cases.
NRO and naval lineages are left for cross-branch reconciliation; unresolved governance candidates have explicit research holds rather than assumed delegated completion.
Current organizational labels on a 2026 webpage are not applied retroactively to historical Department of Defense documents.
centers: This pass screened every named record in the inspected FY2026 current and Historical worksheets, not every entity ever called an FFRDC. The NCSES Historical tab is itself not asserted to be an exhaustive archive of all federal relationships.

FY2024 and FY2025 workbooks were inspected for relevant roster changes. Earlier archived lists linked by NCSES were discovered but not all downloaded/read; do not describe this as a full 1996–2026 archival audit.
The FY2026 workbook contains a name-only NCAR stub in addition to the fully populated NSF NCAR row. Current-center count is 41 populated entries, 42 named rows.

Official roster membership establishes a displayed administrative classification at a stated time, not UAP participation, secrecy practices, access to anomalous material, physical ownership, or original formation date.
FFRDC is not synonymous with GOCO, UARC, a corporation, or a university. GOCO labels here are restricted to DOE laboratories expressly supported by DOE/Sandia descriptions; NETL is GOGO.

Founding, authorization, program start, corporate incorporation, operational start, list entry, renaming, transfer and national-lab designation are distinct. The official defense roster Founded column mixes institutional ancestry with designation history.
IDA communications center origin remains unresolved: defense roster says 1959 while NCSES Historical says existence since 1956. October 1995 master-list addition is represented separately.

CNA center consolidation needs more archival review: GAO 1996 says FFRDC creation in 1961, while institutional accounts commonly use 1962. This output does not choose an unsupported exact consolidation date.
Aerospace corporation incorporation is June 3, 1960; defense roster’s FFRDC Founded label is 1961. An original center charter was not inspected.
NCSES Historical HSSAI row incorrectly names HSSEDI in its phase-out note. HSSEDI remains a distinct current MITRE FFRDC; no closure inferred from the mislabeled note.
NCSES operator-change dates at LANL (June 2018) and SRNL (December 2020) should not be treated as operations handoff dates. DOE/LANL gives November 1, 2018; SRNL history gives 2021, respectively.

SRNL’s own history gives May 7, 2004 national designation and renaming, whereas NCSES Historical gives December 8, 2005 renaming. Both source claims are identified; no false reconciliation is imposed.

PNNL Moments in Time contradicts itself about national-lab designation (mid-1980s versus inception in 1965). Only the clear 1965 Battelle operations transfer and 1995 name change are used as milestones.
Current central UARC roster lists SDL with MDA sponsorship, while SDL’s dated August 11, 2025 announcement names SAF/SQ as new sponsor. Announcement day is not assumed effective transfer day.
UARC roster’s contemporary DoW/USW labels are not projected backwards into WWII or 1990s agency names. Present labels are retained only as displayed roster metadata.

The central UARC page describes a 1996 framework establishment, while its GTRI row and GTRI’s own UARC history use 1995. Those differently scoped dates are not silently reconciled or applied to all centers.

Some sources were accessible through direct public downloads after web-reader failures. These paths are labeled in accessStatus; source passages were read. IDA website pages and an NRC-site history page remained inaccessible; GAO and the NARA NRC administrative history provide inspected alternatives, not search-snippet support.
No universal FOIA exemption, legal immunity, or secrecy claim is made for nonprofits, FFRDCs, UARCs, GOCOs or national laboratories.

No primary source reviewed here supports alien craft possession or reverse engineering. ORNL’s specific AARO-sponsored specimen analysis is a documented role with a terrestrial-result limitation. Psychic-functioning research at SRI/SAIC is kept distinct from UAP claims.

Detailed institutional histories remain uneven: priority laboratories and operators have multiple milestones; other current centers and several UARCs are screening-only profiles with original founding events deferred.
naval-addendum: No UAP involvement is established for these entities. Gerb anonymous-source architectural claims require a separate attributed-claim record.
